question: Mutchler Peak is described as a glacier climb but stored as a scramble: which is right, and what discipline and grade?
answer: Both are partly right; the glacier is the reason to change the discipline. The summit itself is easy: the NE ridge is reached by a third-class heather and duff ramp onto a flat plateau with about 400 ft left to the top (July 2012 solo report: no rope used on Mutchler, no rappel); a June 2026 party took snow from the cirque up the NE ridge with no exposure. But the usual way in is across or beside the Mutchler Glacier: the 2012 report says the ramp puts you right onto the glacier, with gaping cracks; a later party roped up, used crampons and crossed blue ice and a crevasse; and a Mountaineers trip on 3-5 July 2026 turned back because the transition onto the glacier was unsafe. The glacier has shrunk (only the highest north-facing slopes still hold ice), so late-season ascents are scrambles while June to early July is snow and glacier travel. The stored row's own text says 'snow/glacier remnants' and one traverse rappelled a cornice. A comment on a 2026 trip report quotes a guidebook as saying the south shoulder climbs easily, which would be a pure scramble, but I could not confirm an approach to it.
recommendation: Change discipline to alpine (mountaineering is walk-up only and glacier travel is roped, so alpine is the compliant label), grade 'Class 3', keep season Jul-Sep. Add hazards: crevasses and glide cracks on the Mutchler Glacier, cornice on the ridge above Cyclone Lake in early summer; add rope, glacier kit and ice axe for June and early July. If the owner wants a scramble row, it would have to be a separate 'South Shoulder' row, which is unconfirmed.

hazards_add: crevasses and glide cracks on the Mutchler Glacier
cornice on the ridge above Cyclone Lake in early summer
gear_add: rope and glacier kit for the cirque crossing in June and early July
